lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Whoa! Jabu, look at that tree! Its tummy is bigger than yours!
lines.text: Joo! Jabu, sheba sefate seo! Mpa ya sona e kgolo ho feta ya hao!

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Okay, okay. Maybe not bigger. But why is the trunk so wide?
lines.text: Ho lokile, ho lokile. Mohlomong ha e kgolo ho feta. Empa ke hobaneng kutu ya sona e le sephara hakaale?

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: We need berries for our jam. One basket for us, and one little bowl to share.
lines.text: Re hloka monokotshwai bakeng sa jeme ya rona. Seroto se le seng bakeng sa rona, le sekotlolo se senyenyane seo re tla arolelana ka sona.

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Let’s count together. One, two, three, four, five!
lines.text: Ha re baleng mmoho. Nngwe, pedi, tharo, nne, hlano!

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Jabu, your trunk is the fastest berry-picker I’ve ever seen.
lines.text: Jabu, kutu ya hao ke yona e potlakileng ka ho fetisisa ho kga monokotshwai eo nkileng ka e bona.

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: First, bowl. Then berries. Then mash. Then stir. In that order!
lines.text: Pele, sekotlolo. Ebe monokotshwai. Ebe re a silakanya. Ebe re a hlohlelletsa. Ka tatellano eo!

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Catch the purple one! No, the other purple one!
lines.text: Tshwara o pherese! Tjhe, o mong o pherese!

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Well... that did not go to plan.
lines.text: Jwale... hoo ha hoa ka ha tsamaya kamoo re neng re rerile.

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: But we can fix it. We’ll pick up, clean up, and try again.
lines.text: Empa re ka e lokisa. Re tla bokella, re hlwekise, ebe re leka hape.

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: You gather. I sort. Then we both stir.
lines.text: Wena bokella. Nna ke hlophise. Ebe re hlohlelletsa ka bobedi.

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Look! A small pot of jam and a very big adventure.
lines.text: Sheba! Pitsa e nyenyane ya jeme le leeto le leholo haholo.

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Baobabs grow in several parts of Africa. Their thick trunks can store lots of water, which helps them through dry times.
lines.text: Difate tsa baobab di hola dikarolong tse ngata tsa Afrika. Dikutu tsa tsona tse teteaneng di ka boloka metsi a mangata, e leng se di thusang nakong ya komello.

lines.speaker: Lebo
lines.source: Africa is full of different places, people, plants and stories. We’ll discover another one next time.
lines.text: Afrika e tletse dibaka, batho, dimela le dipale tse fapaneng. Re tla sibolla e nngwe nakong e tlang.
